burton_span.exact: but a bad tenant lets it rain in, and for want of reparation fall to decay, &c. translations.text: But when a worthless, careless man moves in, etc. / A storm comes, breaks the tiles and gutters, / the air rots the builder's work, etc. / I will tell you, so that you may think men like houses: / parents, the builders of their children, lay the foundation, / polish them, teach them letters, and spare no expense; / and I, while I was under the builders' control, was a good lad; / but once I moved out into my own nature, / I ruined the builders' work at once and utterly. / Idleness came; that was my storm; / its coming brought hail and rain with it, / it threw down my virtue, etc.
